text: You can train a good model in an afternoon. Six months later, can you say which model is in production, how it scored, and who approved it? The SageMaker Model Registry answers those questions.

The registry has two levels. A model group holds every version built to solve one problem, like churn model. Each version is one registered candidate, numbered automatically. A version does not contain the model. It points to the container image and the model tar gz file in S3.

Every version has an approval status. Pending manual approval, approved, or rejected. With the SageMaker project templates, moving a version to approved can start a deployment pipeline. Rejected does nothing, but the version stays for the audit trail.

Registering is one boto3 call, create model package, naming the group, the status, and an inference specification with the image and model location. This code is adapted from the AWS docs, and it is illustrative. There is no AWS account in this course.

What I did run was an offline check. Using botocore's stubber, I validated four of these requests against boto3's own service model, and a misspelled parameter was rejected. That proves the shape is right. It does not prove AWS will accept your values.

The point of approval is a rule, not a click. Here is a small local sketch in plain Python. It scores three candidates and approves a version only if its A U C is at least point seven five and beats the current one. Superseded is a label in my sketch, not a real status.

To deploy from the registry, call create model with the package's A R N, then create endpoint config, then create endpoint. SDK snippets change between major versions, so check the docs for the one you install. And delete the endpoint when you finish.
Next lesson: what happens after deployment, when the data changes and the model quietly goes stale.
